children.html: S(s)=(s10⋯00s2⋱⋮⋮⋱⋱00⋯0sn).\begin{align*} S(\mathbf{s}) = \begin{pmatrix} s_1 & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & s_2 & \ddots & \vdots \\ \vdots & \ddots & \ddots & 0 \\ 0 & \cdots & 0 & s_n \end{pmatrix}. \end{align*}S(s)=⎝⎛​s1​0⋮0​0s2​⋱⋯​⋯⋱⋱0​0⋮0sn​​⎠⎞​.​

children.value: Since non-zero the entries in this matrix are all in separate rows and columns, the scalar multiplication will be applied to each element of the vector being scaled separately.
If the entries on the diagonal of this matrix are all the same, this is just the same as standard scalar multiplication, since each entry in the vector is multiplied by the same scalar.
To invert the operation of scaling by a vector, the inverse scaling matrix is:

children.html: S−1(s)=(1s10⋯001s2⋱⋮⋮⋱⋱00⋯01sn).\begin{align*} S^{-1}(\mathbf{s}) = \begin{pmatrix} \frac{1}{s_1} & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{s_2} & \ddots & \vdots \\ \vdots & \ddots & \ddots & 0 \\ 0 & \cdots & 0 & \frac{1}{s_n} \end{pmatrix}. \end{align*}S−1(s)=⎝⎛​s1​1​0⋮0​0s2​1​⋱⋯​⋯⋱⋱0​0⋮0sn​1​​⎠⎞​.​
